speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, could you please describe the skin lesions in detail and tell me how long you've had the fever and wrist pain?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: Did you notice any expanding red rash or a "bullseye" lesion at the site of a tick bite during your camping trip? Have you experienced any numbness, tingling, or facial drooping recently?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain in the left wrist. I also have Chills, Malaise, Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on both wrists and hands, Swelling and erythema of the left wrist, Severe tenderness to palpation and passive movement of the left wrist. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Iron deficiency anemia and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: That diagnosis of iron deficiency anemia does not explain your fever, severe wrist pain, or specific skin lesions. Given your recent camping in Minnesota and history of migratory joint pain, I suspect a tick-borne illness like Lyme disease or Rocky Mountain Spotted Fever, but the lesions are atypical. REQUEST TEST: Lyme serology, Rickettsia titers, and joint aspiration for Gram stain and culture.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Joint Aspiration Left Wrist: WBC >50,000 /μL (markedly elevated), Gram Stain: Gram-negative diplococci seen. speaker: Doctor
text: The joint aspiration showing Gram-negative diplococci and the positive gonorrhea test confirm a diagnosis of Disseminated Gonococcal Infection. The classic triad of tenosynovitis, dermatitis, and polyarthralgia fits your presentation perfectly. DIAGNOSIS READY: Disseminated Gonococcal Infection
